plan.curriculum: English 2.0, Level 5: VC2E5LY02 delivering structured spoken texts for a purpose using features of voice; VC2E5LY01 presenting and justifying an opinion; VC2E5LY10 creating spoken texts
plan.shape: model, plan fast, play: the teacher plans and delivers a one-minute speech live, students practise 30-second plans, then play Just a Minute rounds in groups with peer scoring
plan.criticalFeature: claim it, prove it, sell it, say it, in sixty seconds: one claim, two reasons, one action
decisionPoints: the choice check: the strongest one-minute plan
the exit board: a 60-second plan for a new topic
plan.anchor: Claim it. Prove it. Sell it. Say it. Today: all four, in one minute.
plan.catchUp: Anyone can play: the anchor and the plan frame are on the slide.

studentTools: Just a Minute Topic Cards (one set per group of four, cut before the session)
A timer for each group (or the board timer)
routineIcons: Write it, chin it, show me
Point to A, B or C
boardSetup: The 60-second plan: Claim (1 line), Prove (2 reasons), Sell (1 device), Say (an action)
Scoring: one tick each for claim, proof, sell, action

resources.label: Worksheet
resources.description: Your turn: sharpen claims, fix a rambling speech, plan three speeches fast, then write your best one-minute speech.
resources.title: Just a Minute
resources.subtitle: One claim. Two reasons. One action. Sixty seconds.

example.answer: Dogs are the best pets, and I can prove it.

items.prompt: Write a strong one-sentence claim for each topic.
rows: A slide instead of stairs at school
answers: Winter is the best season, no contest.
Every home should have a chore robot.
A slide instead of stairs at school
Every school needs a slide instead of stairs.

steps: Is there an action at the end?
example.answer: If any is missing, the minute is wasted.

options: Claim, then lots of ums, then the bell.
Claim, two reasons, a question, an action.
items.explain: It has every part of the anchor: claim, proof, sell and say.

items.prompt: Ollie's one-minute speech rambled. Find the problem and fix it.
work: So, um, cats. Cats are fluffy. Also my aunty has a cat. Its name is Pickles. Pickles likes fish. Um. Yeah.
items.answer: No clear claim, no real reasons, no action. Fix: Cats are the perfect pet. They're clean and calm. Adopt one this weekend!

example.prompt: Topic: Every class needs a pet.
example.answer: Calm and responsibility; action: vote yes at the class meeting.

rows: Ice cream for breakfast on Fridays
answers: Ice cream for breakfast on Fridays
a reward to look forward to

steps: Sell it with a device, say it with an action
example.answer: Dogs are the best pets. They keep you active. They love you no matter what. Who else greets you like that? Go and adopt one.

items.prompt: Write your best one-minute speech for one topic. Claim it, prove it, sell it, say it.
items.answer: A claim, two reasons, a device and an action, about 100-120 words.

resources.label: Extension
resources.description: Early finisher option: answer comebacks, then argue the side you disagree with.
resources.title: Rebuttal Round
resources.subtitle: The best speakers can argue either side.

example.prompt: Topic: dogs are best. Comeback: dogs are messy.
example.answer: Some say dogs are messy. However, a bit of mud is worth a best friend.

items.prompt: Write a one-line answer to each comeback.
answers: Fit kids learn faster, so it gives time back.
Keep the stairs too; the slide is just faster.
Run a breakfast club before class.

example.prompt: I love winter. Argue for summer.
steps: Pick the side you disagree with
example.answer: Summer means beaches, mangoes and long light evenings. Who could argue with that?

items.prompt: Write a one-minute speech for the side you disagree with. Make it as convincing as you can.
items.answer: A full one-minute speech for the other side, with claim, proof, sell and action.

resources.label: Supported Worksheet
resources.description: Supported option: picture-clue choices, a first plan done and a speech frame.
resources.title: Just a Minute Helper
resources.subtitle: Claim. Two reasons. Action.

example.answer: Pizza Fridays! Tasty and fun. Ask the canteen.

items.hint: The first row is done for you.

example.answer: I think lunch should be longer. Because we need to eat and play. So please give us ten more minutes!

items.prompt: Finish: I think ___. Because ___ and ___. So please ___!
items.answer: A claim, two reasons and an action.

resources.label: Just a Minute Topic Cards
resources.description: Fun activity: twelve silly topics for one-minute speeches. One set per group of four.
resources.title: Just a Minute Topic Cards
resources.subtitle: Draw a card. 30 seconds to plan. 60 seconds to persuade.

cards.text: Kids should choose their own bedtime
Ice cream for breakfast on Fridays
Lunch should be an hour long

slides.notes: Open the session. One line: today is a game. Sixty seconds. One topic. Persuade us.

Print and cut one set of Just a Minute Topic Cards per group of four. Print the Worksheet for everyone, the Extension for early finishers and the Supported Worksheet for those who need it. A visible timer.

slides.learningIntention: We are learning to plan and give a short persuasive speech on the spot.
successCriteria: I can plan a claim and two reasons in 30 seconds.
I can give a one-minute speech that claims it, proves it, sells it and says it.
I can answer a comeback on the spot.

beats: POINT to the learning intention.
SAY: Today is fast and fun. All four moves in sixty seconds.
SAY: Read the I can lines with me. Everyone, together, on three.
SAY: The first one is where we all start.
The second one is today's main goal.
notes.prep: SC1 is reachable for all; SC2 is the core and the exit evidence; SC3 is the stretch.

slides.title: Can your teacher do it?
lines: Pick a topic for me. Any silly topic.
I get 30 seconds to plan and 60 seconds to persuade you.

notes.answer: open - the class scores the teacher on claim, prove, sell, say
beats: SAY: Draw a card for me.
I'll plan for 30 seconds where you can see it.
Then 60 seconds. Score me.
MODEL: plan Claim, two reasons, a device, an action on the board. Then deliver.
ASK: Score me: one finger for each move I did. Claim, prove, sell, say.
5 sec. Cue: Fingers at your chest... show me.
EXPECT: 3 or 4
ASK: Which move did I do best, and which could be better?
15 sec. Turn and tell, partner A first.
EXPECT: good claim; more proof
trap: scoring for funny, not for the moves.
Fix: say funny is a bonus; we score the four moves.
notes.prep: Teacher models live, thinking aloud the plan. Choose a card students can't predict. 4 minutes.

slides.meaning: Done on the spot, with very little time to plan.
slides.example: An impromptu speech: 30 seconds to plan.

notes.answer: done on the spot, with very little time to plan
beats: POINT to the word. SAY: Impromptu. Say it with me. Impromptu.
SAY: Done on the spot, with very little time to plan.
SAY: An impromptu speech: 30 seconds to plan.
ASK: When might you need to speak impromptu in real life?
10 sec. Turn and tell, partner B first.
EXPECT: an interview; a class meeting; when someone asks your opinion
trap: thinking impromptu means no plan at all.
Fix: say a tiny plan is the secret: claim, two reasons, action.

rows: Topic: every class needs a pet
Pets calm us. Caring teaches responsibility.
Who wouldn't learn better next to a guinea pig?
Vote yes at the class meeting!

beats: POINT to Claim it.
SAY: Ten seconds. One sure sentence. No ums before it.
POINT to Prove it.
SAY: Two reasons. Just two. More and you'll run out of time.
POINT to Say it.
SAY: Always finish with what to do. That's how you beat the clock.
ASK: Say the four moves with me.
3 sec. Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
EXPECT: Claim it. Prove it. Sell it. Say it.
trap: spending the whole minute on the first reason.
Fix: say watch the clock; move on at 35 seconds.
notes.stretch: Add a comeback answer in your proof.
notes.help: Hold the plan card while you speak.
notes.prep: The model plan. Critical feature: all four moves, in a minute.

slides.title: Plan it fast
slides.pivot: write the claim first, then any two reasons, then Please...
slides.followUp: cold call one board: say your plan in 20 seconds

items.text: Topic: Every school needs a pool.
items.answer: Claim + two reasons (swimming saves lives; cool in summer) + action

items.text: Topic: Kids should get paid for chores.
items.answer: Claim + two reasons (teaches money; fair) + action

items.text: Topic: The holidays should be longer.
items.answer: Claim + two reasons (rest; family time) + action
Claim + two reasons (comfy reading; calm) + action

items.text: Topic: Every town needs a skate park.
items.answer: Claim + two reasons (active kids; somewhere safe) + action

say: 30 seconds each. Plan, don't write sentences.
trap: writing full sentences and running out of time.
Fix: student writes three or four words per move.
notes.stretch: Add a device to sell it.
notes.help: Use: I think ___ because ___ and ___. Please ___.

options.text: A claim, then lots of ums until the bell.
options.misconception: no proof, no action; the minute is wasted

options.text: A claim, two reasons, a question, an action.

options.misconception: too much proof, no clear side

beats: SAY: Three plans for the same minute.
ASK: Which one-minute plan is strongest?
10 sec. Cue: voices off, everyone points to A, B or C.
EXPECT: pointing to B
SCAN the room, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, cold call: which move is the question?
Less -> match each plan to the four moves, re-ask.
REVEAL after pointing is scanned.
SAY: B. Claim, prove, sell, say. Nothing wasted.
trap: pointing to C because more reasons sounds stronger.
Fix: ask what side are they on? Nobody knows.
notes.prep: Decision point before the game. Under 80% means one more teacher model before groups play.

slides.title: Just a Minute: play!
lines: Groups of four. Draw a card. 30 seconds to plan, 60 to speak.
Listeners score: a tick for claim, prove, sell, say.
Everyone speaks twice. Highest group score wins.

beats: SAY: Draw, plan, speak. The clock is the boss.
TIME each round on the board timer.
CIRCULATE. Note one great claim and one great action to share at the end.
ASK: Thumbs: how did your minute go?
5 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: mostly up after round 2
ASK: Tell your group the best line you heard.
20 sec. Turn and tell, newest speaker first.
EXPECT: a quoted claim or mic drop
trap: Fix: listeners must name the move for every tick.
notes.stretch: Second turn: answer a comeback from a listener mid-speech.
notes.help: Speak with the plan card in hand; first turn can be 30 seconds.
notes.prep: Fun activity: impromptu speaking game. 16 minutes, two rounds. SC2 and SC3.

slides.title: Write your best minute
slides.task: Work through your Worksheet. Finish by writing your best one-minute speech in full.

notes.answer: a one-minute speech with claim, two reasons, a device and an action
beats: POINT to the task.
SAY: Take your best game topic and write it properly.
SAY: Read the task, complete each part, check your work.
Finished? Extension next. Everyone, together, on three.
CIRCULATE. Ask: where's your action? Could you say it in a minute?
ASK: Time your partner reading their speech. Under a minute?
60 sec each. Turn and tell, partner A first.
EXPECT: 50 to 70 seconds
trap: a written speech that is three minutes long.
Fix: student cuts to two reasons and one device.
notes.stretch: Extension: answer comebacks, then argue the other side.
notes.help: Supported Worksheet: picture-clue choices, a first plan done, a frame.
notes.prep: Independent application of the full anchor; Week 8 starts the real speech. SC2.

slides.extendedTask: a worksheet ending in a written one-minute speech

slides.title: Show what you know
questions: New topic: Every family should have a vegetable patch.
Write your 60-second plan: claim, two reasons, an action.

notes.answer: e.g. Claim; fresh food and less waste; plant one thing this weekend
beats: SAY: A new topic. Plan it like the game.
ASK: Write your 60-second plan.
60 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: a claim, two reasons, an action
RECORD who misses the action. Week 8 conference list.
trap: a claim and five reasons, no action.
Fix: none now, record the name.
notes.prep: Exit evidence for SC2 on a new topic. One board per student.

slides.reflectionPrompt: What will you take from today into writing your real speech next week?

notes.answer: open - always finish with an action
beats: SAY: Let's read our I can lines together. Everyone, together, on three.
ASK: How sure are you that you can claim,
prove, sell and say it in a minute?
5 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: thumbs up, sideways or down
RECORD each thumb down beside the exit boards.
ASK: What will you take from today
into writing your real speech next week?
20 sec. Turn and tell, partner B first.
EXPECT: always finish with an action
notes.prep: End of Week 7. Next week: students write their own speeches. SC2.
